proposals.before: Zhilugu, Wang Bai, and Yelü Diru committed no great wrongs or merits — it is right that they be recorded.
proposals.after: Zhilugu, Wang Bai, and Yelü Diru had neither great merits nor demerits — it is right that they be recorded.
proposals.reason: 得失 means gains/losses or merits/demerits; 'committed no great wrongs or merits' is unnatural and obscures the sense.

proposals.before: Under Taizong he served as an imperial physician in attendance.
proposals.after: In Taizong's time he served as an imperial physician in attendance.
proposals.reason: 'Under Taizong' is awkward as a sentence opener and can be misread as a personal name; the Chinese is 太宗時.

decisions.reason: 無大得失 means they had no great merits or demerits (gains or losses); 'committed no great wrongs or merits' misrenders 得失 and pairs 'committed' with merits unnaturally. The proposed 'neither great merits nor demerits' matches the Chinese and is natural English.
太宗時 is accurately rendered by the established historiographical idiom 'Under Taizong'; the proposed 'In Taizong's time' is only a stylistic alternate, not a correction of error.
